name: Joey Clerk
caption: Isamu League's own promoter, presenting the fed as his own return to the ring business after an earlier promotion's 2008 closure.

tenures.source: The fed's own founding documents (League Charter sub-forum, 20 January 2010) and both served broadcasts (Lesson 1, Lesson 2), all served under this wing.

name: Nate Narwin
caption: Isamu League's own colour commentator, a former Shootclub Wrestling Alliance United States Champion who twice turned an off-script attack into an official, ranking-points-counting win.

tenures.source: The fed's own staff-cast document (20 January 2010) and both served broadcasts, all served under this wing.

name: Riddick
caption: "The Reckoner," "Mr. RSW," a returning veteran wrestler who lost Isamu League's own first main event by submission and answered with a post-match assault, then fought goldFISH to a time-limit draw on Lesson 2.

tenures.source: The fed's own roster application (2 February 2010) and both served broadcasts, all served under this wing.

identity.note: Three held characters elsewhere in the museum carry the word "Riddick" as part of a longer, decorated name (a surname or middle name paired with a distinct given name). This wing's own wrestler is billed under the bare single name "Riddick" throughout, with no shared given name, hometown, era, or promotion to any of the three, so no join is asserted; the mint guard's own decorated-substring check is expected to flag the coincidence and this note answers it in advance.

name: Randall Beetwix
caption: A veteran, forty-two-year-old wrestler chasing one last shot at the top after his prior promotion folded before he could become its champion; he won Isamu League's first match, then twisted his ankle on the way out.

tenures.source: The fed's own roster application (30 January 2010) and the Lesson 1 broadcast, plus two served roleplays, all served under this wing.

name: AK-47
caption: A former United States Marine and independent-circuit brawler whose bar-area brawl on Isamu League's first broadcast got him arrested and cost him his own scheduled match.

tenures.source: The fed's own roster application (8 February 2010) and the Lesson 1 broadcast, both served under this wing.

name: Naoki Inoue
caption: A nineteen-year-old high-flying prospect nicknamed "Diamond Child," awarded a forfeit win when his scheduled opponent was arrested, then attacked and defeated by the fed's own colour commentator on the same broadcast.

tenures.source: The fed's own roster application (11 February 2010) and the Lesson 1 broadcast, both served under this wing.

name: Masaharu Keichigawa
caption: A Japanese wrestler whose scheduled Lesson 1 match never happened after a backstage confrontation with his own opponent turned into a real fight.

tenures.source: The fed's own roster application (26 January 2010) and the Lesson 1 broadcast, both served under this wing.

name: Jun Nakagawa
caption: A Japanese power wrestler modeled on visiting gaijin brawlers, whose scheduled Lesson 1 match never happened after a backstage confrontation with his own opponent turned into a real fight.

tenures.source: The fed's own roster application (28 January 2010) and the Lesson 1 broadcast, both served under this wing.

name: Xander Thomas
caption: A wrestler who applied to Isamu League's own roster in late March 2010 but never appeared on a broadcast before the promotion's own hiatus.

tenures.source: The fed's own roster application (27 March 2010), served under this wing; no later document mentions this character.

name: Goro Yamashi
caption: Isamu League's own financial backer, a Japanese socialite who unveiled the fed's own championship belt at a press conference in his only appearance in the held record.

tenures.source: The fed's own staff-cast document (20 January 2010) and a served news article on the title-belt unveiling (31 January 2010), both served under this wing.

name: Kyo Miyagi
caption: Isamu League's own play-by-play commentator, calling both of the fed's served broadcasts.

tenures.source: The fed's own staff-cast document (20 January 2010) and both served broadcasts, all served under this wing.

name: Hideki Koga
caption: Isamu League's own studio host, opening and closing both of the fed's served broadcasts from its Tokyo headquarters.

tenures.source: The fed's own staff-cast document (20 January 2010) and both served broadcasts, all served under this wing.

name: Cho Takahashi
caption: Isamu League's own backstage interviewer, reporting live from a trashed medical room on Lesson 1's own broadcast.

tenures.source: The fed's own staff-cast document (20 January 2010) and the Lesson 1 broadcast, both served under this wing.

name: T.K. "Tiger" Tanaka
caption: Isamu League's own ring announcer, a four-time former champion of the fed's own claimed predecessor promotion, introducing every match on both served broadcasts.

tenures.source: The fed's own staff-cast document (20 January 2010) and both served broadcasts, all served under this wing.

name: Shin Sasaki
caption: Isamu League's own senior referee, officiating the main event of the fed's first broadcast.

tenures.source: The fed's own staff-cast document (20 January 2010, spelled "Shin Sasake") and the Lesson 1 broadcast (spelled "Shin Sasaki"), both served under this wing.

name: Nori Tanaka
caption: Isamu League's own "second referee," who called the fed's own impromptu opening-night match between its colour commentator and a young prospect.

tenures.source: The fed's own staff-cast document (20 January 2010) and the Lesson 1 broadcast, both served under this wing.

name: Miki Mochizuka
caption: Isamu League's own female referee, officiating the feature bout of the fed's second broadcast.

tenures.source: The fed's own staff-cast document (20 January 2010) and the Lesson 2 broadcast, both served under this wing.

name: Akio Sato
caption: Isamu League's own interviewer, described in the fed's own staff-cast document but not seen active in either broadcast read this pass.

tenures.source: The fed's own staff-cast document (20 January 2010), served under this wing; no later document shows this character active.
